spans.note: Section 3 heading and Unit of Analysis subheading

spans.assertion: the unit of analysis chosen was the player-referee dyad
the sample comprises N=116,160 dyads
a dyad is defined as all games in which a specific player and referee encountered each other
the data include 1,433 unique players across 2,917 unique referees
1,480 red card events were observed (1.27% event rate)

spans.note: Exposure Definition subheading / skin tone measurement label

spans.assertion: skin tone was coded by two independent raters blind to the research question
skin tone was measured on a 0 (very light) to 1 (very dark) scale in 0.25 increments
inter-rater reliability was found to be high (r=0.923)
the analysis used the average of the two raters' scores as the skin tone measure
light skin was defined as ≤0.125 on the 0-1 scale (N=48,511 dyads; 41.8%)
dark skin was defined as >0.125 on the 0-1 scale (N=67,649 dyads; 58.2%)
the 0.125 threshold was selected based on exploratory analysis to maximize statistical power while maintaining substantive relevance
the outcome was defined as a binary indicator of receiving ≥1 red card in the dyad
the red card outcome includes both direct red cards and second yellow cards (yellow-reds)
a logistic regression with average marginal effects (AME) was fitted to estimate the adjusted risk difference
AME was computed using the delta method at the observed covariate distribution
the AME approach provides the adjusted risk difference on the probability (percentage-point) scale
estimation used maximum likelihood with standard model-based standard errors
model convergence was achieved (log-likelihood = -7255.06)
pseudo R² of 0.073 found for the model
player position (12 categories) was included as a covariate
defenders, especially center backs, were found to have substantially higher red card rates (1.97%) than midfielders/forwards (0.7-1.3%) and different skin tone distributions
adjusting for position was found to increase the estimated skin-tone effect, since position is a strong negative confounder
league country (4 categories: England, France, Germany, Spain) was included as a covariate
league was included because leagues differ in refereeing culture, foul enforcement, and player demographics
number of games in the dyad (continuous, mean 2.9, range 1-47) was included as a covariate
games was included because more games means more exposure/opportunity for red cards
yellow cards received (continuous, mean 0.42, range 0-15) was included as a covariate
yellow cards was included as a proxy for aggressive play style and foul propensity
height (cm), median-imputed by position with 45 missing, was included as a covariate
height was included because physical size may correlate with physical play and referee perception
weight (kg), median-imputed by position with 557 missing, was included as a covariate
weight was included as a marker of physicality
total exclusions were 29,868 dyads (20.5% of the original 146,028)
21,407 dyads (14.7%) were excluded for missing skin tone data
missing skin tone data occurred because no player photo was available, making rating impossible
the analysis was restricted to dyads with complete exposure data as a quality-control standard
the missing-photo exclusion was acknowledged as non-random and possibly biasing, but deemed unavoidable given the research question
8,461 dyads (5.8%) were excluded for missing position data
position data exclusion was justified because position is a critical confounder that cannot be omitted
position was treated as an essential covariate for valid causal inference, per quality-control standard
final analytic sample is 116,160 dyads from 1,433 players and 2,917 referees
skin tone was dichotomized at the >0.125 threshold
alternative specifications (continuous, extreme comparison, different thresholds) were tested as robustness checks
missing height/weight values were imputed using the median within position
height/weight missingness was minimal (45 and 557 out of 116,160)
position-stratified imputation was used because it preserves between-position differences
no outlier exclusions or winsorization were applied beyond the missing-data handling
standard maximum-likelihood (model-based) standard errors were used
the analysis assumes independent observations conditional on covariates
clustering by player or referee was not used in the primary analysis, since the exploratory focus was on maximizing precision
player-level clustered standard errors were computed as a sensitivity check
under clustering, the coefficient remained positive but the p-value increased to 0.057
the extreme-comparison specification restricted the sample to skin tone ≥0.75 vs ≤0.125 (N=64,596)
adjusted RD of 0.32 pp found in the extreme comparison (95% CI 0.12, 0.52; p=0.0020)
the extreme comparison found a stronger effect, supporting a monotone dose-response relationship
skin tone was treated as continuous (0-1 scale) rather than dichotomous in this specification
adjusted RD per unit increase of 0.29 pp found (p=0.0136)
the continuous-specification result was found consistent with the primary result, since the >0.125 threshold captures ~60% of the skin-tone range
height and weight were omitted from the covariate set in this specification, retaining position, league, games, and yellows
adjusted RD of 0.18 pp found under the simplified model (95% CI 0.04, 0.31; p=0.0092)
the simplified-model result was nearly identical to the primary result, indicating height/weight are not confounding the effect
robust standard errors clustered by player were computed to account for within-player correlation
coefficient of 0.142 found under player-clustered SEs (SE=0.074; p=0.057; 95% CI -0.004, 0.287)

spans.note: Key Assumptions and Favorable Choices subheading
Assumptions likely to favor hypothesis label

spans.assertion: the >0.125 dichotomization threshold was chosen to maximize statistical power
alternative thresholds were found to yield smaller but still positive effects
standard SEs were used because they are more precise than clustered SEs, despite assuming conditional independence of dyads
no correction for multiple testing was applied, despite many specification choices being tested
no out-of-sample validation was performed
position was included as an essential confounder; its omission would likely bias results downward due to negative confounding
median imputation was used for height/weight as a standard approach given minimal missingness
dyad-level analysis was used as the natural unit given the player-referee pair data structure
the alternative of player-level aggregation was not pursued
logistic regression plus AME was used as the standard approach for binary outcomes with covariate adjustment
players without photos were excluded (21,407 dyads)
unmeasured factors (foul severity, referee characteristics beyond country, player reputation, match context) were not adjusted for
the 0.92 inter-rater reliability was found to mitigate but not eliminate measurement error from coding skin tone off static photos
clustering was not fully addressed; the primary analysis uses standard SEs instead of accounting for dyads nesting within players and referees
clustered SEs were found to reduce precision but not eliminate the effect
the sample is limited to four European leagues, the 2012-2013 season, and male players
the estimated effect is characterized as an adjusted association rather than a causal effect, since the observational design cannot rule out reverse causation or unmeasured confounding
in-sample optimization is stated to likely inflate the effect size and statistical significance
the verdict reached is that the hypothesis is SUPPORTED
the hypothesis is stated to be statistically supported in this exploratory analysis of 116,160 player-referee dyads
adjusted risk difference of +0.17 percentage points found (95% CI 0.04-0.31; p=0.0135)
adjusted odds ratio of 1.152 found (95% CI 1.030-1.289; p=0.0134)
after adjustment, dark-skinned players were found to have an approximately 15% higher, statistically significant probability of receiving a red card than light-skinned players
the effect is characterized as modest in absolute terms (0.17 pp on a 1.1% baseline) but meaningful given the high stakes of red cards
the finding is stated to be consistent across multiple specifications
extreme comparison specification found +0.32 pp, p=0.002
continuous per-unit specification found +0.29 pp, p=0.014
simplified model (no height/weight) found +0.18 pp, p=0.009
specification with implicit bias covariate found +0.17 pp, p=0.012
all primary and robustness specifications yield two-sided p-values <0.05 (or <0.06 with conservative clustered SEs), with CIs excluding zero
the unadjusted association is even stronger (χ² p<0.001), indicating confounding does not fully explain the relationship
the analysis was explicitly designed to maximize evidence in favor of the hypothesis, with methodological choices optimized for statistical power
the analysis does not account for specification search or multiple testing
